In the summer time, cracking open a juicy lobster is just the beginning of your stay in Shediac… a vacation paradise for people of all tastes!

In the winter time, you can just walk behind this cozy house and get to the Shediac arena on the next street in just minutes to get to your kids' hockey tournaments or just enjoy family skating and many more winter attractions!
neighborhood_overview:
Approximately 5 minutes away by car, you will be able to take a dip at the famous Parlee Beach Provincial Park, one of North America's finest beaches and home of the warmest salt water in Canada. With waters peaking at 24 degrees Celcius (75 degrees Fahrenheit), it is the warmest water north of Virginia. This park also includes a supervised swimming beach, volleyball, ultimate Frisbee, football, a sand-sculpture competition, and daily scheduled sports activities.

Two marinas are also situated in the Shediac area; the downtown Shediac Bay Yatch Club Marina and the Point du Chêne Marina where you can rent boats, visit boutiques and the Homarus Eco-Centre, fish on the wharf with the locals, and purchase boat cruises.

host_about:
The accent is still pure "Yankee" despite the fact that Danny and Gael Ryan, toting their 2 small children, immigrated to the Canadian Maritimes well over 40 years ago. Gael, whose strong Canadian roots are connected to her father and maternal grandparents, always had "living in Canada" in the back of her mind since she was a child visiting the many relatives in the area every summer. Both her father and grandparents had emigrated in the 1920's from Canada to New England, where both Danny and Gael were brought up and educated. Danny, a heavy equipment operator, had only a wee bit of carpentry experience and Gael was the artistic half of the duo. After marriage and 2 young children it was decided to give up the 9-5 lifestyle and "move to the country' (albeit another country!) Danny was always fond of remarking "Gael, we don't have to move THIS FAR to be out in the country!" in March 1975, with all the immigration requirements behind them, they arrived at the old farmhouse they’d purchased 2 years earlier....let's take a look back on that traumatic experience...

In 1973 when Danny and Gael first glimpsed the weathered gray Greek Revival house in a snowy New Brunswick field, one of many ensuing differences of opinion permeated the air. Gael said (after crawling over 2 feet of frozen debris) "look! I can have a huge Christmas tree! The ceilings are so high!" Danny said "NEVER! I am getting the H-LL out of here! I wouldn't take this dump if they gave it to me!" The 1841 abandoned house was textbook derelict due to the leaky tin roof (flapping in a stiff breeze); the knee deep debris which had been wet and then frozen to every floor throughout, nearly 300 small broken panes of glass (the object of local target practice); the wet horsehair plaster hanging in shards from all ceilings and wall surfaces; 2 rooms of complete sooty blackness from previously rusted stovepipes; barn swallow nests on every door and window corner; no electricity and the "plumbing" consisted of a frozen cracked cast iron hand pump and an "outhouse" with 2 back walls missing! But, according to Gael's grandmother, who had accompanied them to view the property, “the roof line is perfectly straight, Danny" and if you want to buy it, I'll help you fix it!" With prompting from "Nana" (an expert carpenter in her own right) Danny was reluctantly persuaded to go along with the idea — a week and $2000 later the wreck of the house and 25 acres belonged to them! With no clue where to begin, Danny simply boarded up all the broken windows with cheap paneling until they could return from Massachusetts in August to begin the daunting task (with the expert help from Nana, of course!) Unfortunately, when Nana returned to Massachusetts she decided to marry her second husband, an elderly neighbor, and that was the end of the expert advice on even where to begin fixing the wreck. In August, upon returning to the "fixer-upper" for his 2 week "vacation" Danny happily tore off the warped paneling —which only exposed the full extent of the disastrous real estate deal! Because the paneling closed out not only the snow and rain, but also the sun and wind, and hot august temperatures had created a moldering melted mess and all the filthy knee deep debris was a rotting mass of slimy junk. Danny was horrified when he glimpsed what the removal of the paneling and daylight had exposed inside the wrecked shell of a house. "What have we done????" he groaned "it will be so beautiful when it's done! Just wait and see!" said Gael (as she carefully averted her eyes so he couldn't see her tears running down her face ,inwardly crying "Dear God, what have I gotten us into???" of course she would NEVER admit she had talked him into such a disastrous deal!)

Well, first things first-how to empty the pathetic shell of a house of all the moldy filth...having brought with them only the most rudimentary tools (hammer, handsaw, screwdrivers, and a couple of shovels) they waded into the disgusting mess with the vigor only a young and foolish couple could muster in the face of such adversity. During the first several days they discovered the most effective way to distribute the wet interior filth was to drag it out to a freshly hand-dug pit and dump it, so they madly shoveled the slimy mess into the bottoms of 2 old broken trunks, trussed themselves up as beasts of burden dragging the trunks behind them. Several hundred trips later the actual pumpkin pine floors and stairs were exposed and found to be in excellent condition (not rotted, although wet and stained). After the floors were exposed all the wet blackened plaster was then removed and carted out to the pit. Next, they replaced nearly 300 small window panes —very time consuming and Danny still planned to put an asphalt shingle roof on the house all before they went back to Massachusetts . They actuality accomplished all they’d set out to do I As they worked tirelessly, they were very thankful for an obliging auntie who gave them ,after each exhausting 16 hour day, bed and board and babysitting and much excellent "hardware and building supply store" advice! Then back to Massachusetts to scrimp and save for the next onslaught the following summer-arriving with gallons of paint, wallpaper, and miscellaneous goods to work for another 2 weeks. During this "vacation" time, after replacing the gutted plaster walls and ceilings with sheet rock, Danny rented an industrial floor sander and sanded all the floors and varnished them— they were lovely! Gael busily wallpapered all the rooms. Although there was still no plumbing, for electricity they had one plug-in and one dangling lite bulb (a modern miracle!) run in by a local electrician. They worked with a 3 legged table and a broken down ladder to further their second summer's accomplishments.

By fall of 1974 they had gone through the immigration process in Boston and planned to move in March of 1975 (one of the worst winters on record in this area) it wasn't pretty!! Optimistically packed with all their earthly possessions for the new adventure of the "dream house," the large U-Haul truck drove out of a dandelion infested Massachusetts spring into a literal blanket of snow at the Canadian border. Arriving at the end of their Maritime driveway they were faced with a wall of ice and snowdrift so large that it took an industrial strength snow blower to clear the path to get into the yard. And in the yard....snowy ground littered with asphalt shingle tabs which had blown off the new roof (too late they learned that "peel-n-stick" shingle tabs DO NOT work on a Maritime roof (one needs to individually tar down every shingle as it goes on.) When at last they gained admittance to the dream house, their hearts dropped yet again! The snow had sifted through the badly set glass panes and snow drifts inside the house had to be shoveled out before anything could be unloaded. The 55 rolls of beautiful documentary wallpaper was lying in crystalline sheets on the varnished floors where it had peeled off the frost infested walls earlier during the winter. There was no wood to use in the crummy $35 wood stove (hooked up to a rather crumbly chimney) they had installed as an after thought in the previous August, and the plumbing was still non-existent. The furniture and food was unloaded in a central location, yet out of the way of the many unexpected problems they were encountering at every tum. Danny concluded that the most urgent requirement was a reliable source of heat inside the sub-zero "barn" that the house had become. They burned any wooden debris they could salvage, broken furniture and 2 interior walls in the old kitchen ell until they were able to get a truckload of slab wood delivered in the inclement conditions.

Although totally unprepared for the disaster the "dream house" had evolved into since their last efforts in the previous summer, Danny refused to leave the premises for another 2 weeks while he reworked the many amateur mistakes they'd made earlier. Even on the coldest of nights when Gael and the children would be warmly ensconced nightly with the dear auntie and her family, he stoically slept in the ice encrusted bedroom (with a wrapped hot brick to warm the bed) where even his beard froze around his mouth during the bone chilling nights. After Danny's managing to acquire some semblance of order to the house, Gael and the children moved back to the house for good-all 4 of them living in borrowed ski-doo suits for the next 2 months (with auntie kindly providing hot showers and laundry service as needed) they encountered at least a dozen major blizzards during the next 2 months; melting the abundant snow for all their water needs-living like pioneers. In the late spring Danny hand dug a septic field and installed a real bathroom and kitchen sink with the advice of a local retired plumber. By the following fall an oil furnace was installed which thrilled them no end! They then opened a small antiques shop in the old kitchen ell which eventually became the delightful “country decorator holiday house" when it was moved off the main house in 1981. This may be where YOU come in!!!

neighborhood_overview: Though the village of Alma is small, don't underestimate all that it has to offer! Located on the coast of the beautiful Bay of Fundy, at the base of the Fundy National Park, and a short drive to a few of New Brunswick's must see attractions like the Hopewell Rocks, there is no shortage of things to see and do. A walk through the village will take you to a variety of restaurants, a fish market, gift shops and the fisherman's wharf where you can see fisherman offloading fresh seafood and view the rise and fall of the highest tides in the world. You can walk the ocean floor during low tide at Alma Beach and beachcomb for shells, fossils and other treasures. neighborhood_overview:
Cast Away is secluded but you are only minutes away from the Village of Blackville where you will find a grocery store, liquor store, hardware store, post office, and pharmacy in addition to a number of restaurants.

The City of Miramichi is a short 30 minute drive.

Blackville Municipal Park features enchanting walking trails, a playground, picnic area, boat launch, splash pad, pavilion and an observation deck.

Outdoor enthusiasts will be happy to know Cast Away is just minutes away from a dedicated ATV and Snowmobile trail. You can even walk-it, bike-it, or hike-it.

Canoe rentals, kayak rentals and tube rentals nearby.

Adventure awaits!
host_about:
Hi….I’m Beth.  I’m a “military brat” who lived and travelled all over the world growing up.  Many of my summers were spent on the Mighty Miramichi, where my mom and generations before her were born.  I loved spending time with my Grandparents here, and have many fond memories of these New Brunswick summers. 
My Uncle and Aunt recently moved back to the Miramichi and ventured into the vacation rental business.  They opened up Cast Away Vacation rentals in May of 2020 and have thoroughly enjoyed helping guests create special and memorable vacations on the beautiful Miramichi River.
My husband Mike and I (with our three children) have decided to jump on board with the intent to carry on creating these exciting experiences for guests at the Lodge and at our newest property the Grand Lodge. 
We are pleased and proud to be assuming the reins of Cast Away Vacation Rentals in September of 2022.  We look forward to hosting you, your family and friends very soon!!!
~Beth and Mike

name: The Carriage House - Tranquility & Stunning View
description:
Situated directly on the coastline of Passamaquoddy Bay, nestled within 28 acres, the Carriage House offers a unique opportunity for relaxation, solace and stunning sunsets.

You will have spectacular views of the Bay and across to St. Andrews and Ministers Island.

Walk to our beach to explore the beautiful coastline and experience the dramatic Fundy tides (Up to 21ft between high/low water), or relax on the large deck watching the bald eagles glide by. A birders paradise.
neighborhood_overview:
We are close by to the fishing village of Back Bay, and Greens Point Lighthouse & Museum.

Drive aboard the free Deer Island car ferry, a 5 minute drive away, for a trip to Deer Island, where the incredible tidal current of the Bay of Fundy creates unlimited adventure. While on the island be sure to visit Deer Island Point Park and Eagle Shadow Hiking Trail at Chocolate Cove for breathtaking views and some lovely spots to have a picnic.

St George with its supermarket, butchers and pub is a 15 minute drive away. St Andrews (whale watching, restaurants and shopping etc) and the border town of St. Stephen are about 35 minutes drive away. Saint John is an hour away.

name: Home with a spectacular view!
description:
Our old family homestead is waiting for you! From the wrap-around veranda, enjoy a "Million Dollar View" of the majestic expanse of the Shepody Marshes, Mary's Point Bird Sanctuary and Grindstone Island. Nicely located in rural NB, just 10 km from the Hopewell Rocks, 24 km from Cape Enrage, 13 km from Shepody National Wildlife area (Mary's Point), and 32 km to Fundy National Park.
Saw Mill Creek Covered Bridge and walking trails are just a minute away.
neighborhood_overview:
Bring your kayaks and bikes to this destination because both opportunities are a hop, skip, and jump away!
A family style restaurant (including seafood! and gluten free meals) is a short 5 minute drive away.
Liquor store, pharmacy, gas station with take out meals are within a 5 minute drive.
This property is located within 10 minutes of the world famous Hopewell Rocks where you can explore the ocean floor by foot at low tide and by kayak at high tide.
Fundy National Parks offers dozens of hiking trails, beaches and a beautiful golf course.
The village of Alma, outside Fundy National Park, has shops, restaurants, a micro brewery and fresh lobster direct from the fisherman (seasonally).
Cape Enrage with its beautiful lighthouse and fog horn dating back to 1838 offers adventures including rapelling, zip-lining, obstacle course and a beach walk at low tide.

This cottage is all about location, comfort and open space. And in true Maritime charm, it takes on a feeling of home for anyone who stays here. Enjoy time with your loved ones, including your furry ones, at The Crew’s Nest Cottage.

After a day at the beach, walk back home within minutes and spend the evening BBQing and lounging on the back deck. Whether you’re coming as a couple or as a family, The Crew’s Nest Cottage will be sure to suit your needs perfectly.
neighborhood_overview:
Your family will enjoy a 5 minute walk to the warmest salt waters North of the Carolina’s, and a 10 minute walk to the charming Pointe-Du-Chêne wharf. Here you’ll find ice-cream shops, restaurants, bars, art galleries and gift shops. You’ll also find the fun Ecocentre Homarus Eco-Centre, the lighthouse, and cruise tours.

Only a few minutes drive away is the quaint town of Shediac for groceries, gas stations, restaurants, hardware stores and so much more.

neighborhood_overview:
Cocagne is a quaint seaside village still reminiscent of family getaways, good seafood and strikingly beautiful nature. Step back in time and experience the Acadian coast the way it’s been enjoyed for decades.

Just a short drive to Bouctouche where you'll find the "Irving Nature Park Sand Dune" which is a protected boardwalk beach area, and the "Pays de la Sanguine" a fun historical village. Kouchibouguac National Park is beyond Bouctouche where you can rent fat tire bikes to ride through the trees or a kayak or canoe to experience the lakes and beaches!

In the other direction, Cocagne is just down the road with its charming seaside vibes. Shediac is a short drive away for lots of fresh caught eats and NB's most popular public beach - Parlee! Further along is Moncton with all the amenities one could ask for such as a waterpark, zoo, casino, shopping and spas! Keep going and you'll end up at Fundy National Park and Hopewell Rocks for the highest tides in the worl

Myrtle's Pizza is a local favorite for take out and eat on the cottage deck, or head to the Bay Breeze in Pocologan for east coast fare on their ocean front patio in a casual setting. Head down the street at low tide to a family & dog friendly beach to search for sea glass, sand dollars and hermit crabs.  The basin peninsula is a great place for a short walk, or to launch sea kayaks, and bird watch. Bald eagles nest annually on the islands, and often fly over head.

description:
Located in the heart of the village of Riverside-Albert, this thoughtfully renovated heritage house is the perfect place to use as a home base for your Bay of Fundy adventures. The world famous Hopewell Rocks are a short drive as well.

neighborhood_overview:
The Kingston Historic District is a rare example of a rural centre that has existed since the late 18th century. In 2000, Kingston was designated a historic district under the Province of New Brunswick’s Historic Sites Protection Act. The village was settled in 1783 by Loyalists at the conclusion of the American Revolution. The District is recognized for being a rare surviving example of a rural village which has served the spiritual, commercial and educational needs of the surrounding area since the 1780s.

All of the important buildings befitting a community’s social centre are still present. The prominent positions of the church, school and general store are key elements to the Kingston Historic District.

name: Waterfront Retreat, Beach, Pool & Nat'l Park!
description:
Enjoy the spectacular views of sparkling waters, birds and boats from this beautiful waterfront beach-house!
Stroll along your backyard beach, take a dip in the resort-shared pool and hot tub, grill fresh-caught eats on the BBQ, make memories at the fire-pit, catch the sunset and be dazzled by the stars.
Breathe in summer at it's best! Take a short drive to Kouchibouguac Nat'l Park for EPIC hikes, kayaks and fat bikes! Enjoy small town flavour at this relaxing & refreshing waterfront re-treat!
neighborhood_overview:
Perfectly located 15 minutes from the National Park of Kouchibouguac for hikes, kayaking and fat bikes, 10 minutes to boat tours to see the seals and dunes, 20 minutes to the Bouctouche Sand Dunes, Pays de la Sagouine, Golf Courses. Just 45 minutes to the Hub of the Maritimes, Moncton offers Shopping, Dining, Casino, Spas, the fun filled Magnetic Hill and Water Park. At just over an hour's drive you'll find the world famous Hopewell Rocks boasting the highest tides in the world! This chalet has everything to keep you exploring or simply enjoying the view from this unique perspective in paradise.

Enjoy all the local attractions around such as the Marina, the Fisherman's Wharf, Boutiques, Shops and local Restaurants. Take a short walk to the quaint downtown of Richibucto for some ice-cream, fresh-caught lobster and other Maritime home cooking!

The chalet is located on a Resort Chalet Pointe! It offers offers private beaches, amazing amenities including a shared poo
host_about:
As a host with a young family who loves to travel when possible, I strive to create memorable experiences for my guests who visit our little slice of paradise. I make myself available to recommend local experiences and to enhance your stay however possible. I can also leave you your space and allow you to soak up the good times!

I look forward to hosting you and making you feel at home. 

We strive for you to have a 5 star stay!
Warmest regards!

name: *Once Upon a Tide* Waterfront Escape
description:
Welcome to Once Upon a Tide. We are located on a quiet road on the water's edge in Cocagne; a charming village along the Acadian Coast. Our newly renovated private waterfront cottage is located on an acre of land with an amazing panoramic view of Cocagne Bay and is perfect for vacations, weekend getaways, and special occasions for families, couples, or friends meeting up on the east coast.
Experience comfort and tranquility, while still enjoying many close tourist destinations.
neighborhood_overview:
Cocagne was named after Cockaigne, a mythical paradise meaning "land of abundance" in medieval French literature. It is located at the mouth of the Cocagne River on the Northumberland Strait and was founded in 1767.

Cocagne is a peaceful coastal village with all amenities around. We are 3 minutes from the grocery store, take-out restaurants, and gas station plus close to the pharmacy. We are conveniently located between Parlee Beach in Shediac and La Dune de Bouctouche. You can enjoy both with a short drive :)
host_about:
My husband and I live in beautiful Grand Barachois NB with our three kids and our big English Lab. We originally bought our cottage to renovate for my parents to live in but plans quickly changed as we were recently blessed with another sweet boy. 

We are big travel and outdoor enthusiasts and try to discover new places often and like to think of ourselves as savvy travellers. 

We are trying to bring up our children to value experiences over "things" and have discovered what we can't live without (besides my family itself) being by the water, sunsets and sunshine. 

We know very well what it's like to be a traveller so we will try to be as accommodating as possible with our guests. We have strong roots in the Maritimes and have lived in multiple cities so please don't hesitate to ask for recommendations!

I look forward to hosting you and making you feel at home and am available for any questions at all times.

I would also like to welcome you to New Brunswick, to our beautiful slice of Paradise :)

Please have a great stay!

name: Serenity By The Sea: The Coleman Cottage
description:
Looking for a cozy place to stay this spring and summer with all the amenities?

We have it here!

We are located in downtown Alma; walking distance to all the restaurants, shops, grocery store. We are only steps away from the beach featuring the tides of the Bay of Fundy and the beautiful Fundy National Park.

neighborhood_overview:
The cottage was originally built in 1884 and was located in Point Wolfe in Fundy Park. It arrived at its present location on a barge that floated down the bay. Today it is located along the Upper Salmon River which is fed by the Bay of Fundy as the tide comes in right in downtown Alma. There are lots of homes/cottages/restaurants etc in the immediate area, and you are only seconds away from the entry to Fundy Park. You will need a park pass if you plan to enjoy all the park has to offer - In the summer, you have the pool, lakes, biking, hiking, fishing and exploring! In the winter months you will find our location at the base of the snow mobile trail on one end of the street and the gas station/corner store on the other end. We also have a large driveway that's perfect for parking your sleds.
There are also many other winter activities available, snow shoeing, cross country skiing, and often the ice skating rink in town is ready to go!

description:
Welcome to our well equipped, modern cottage. This property holds an amazing Bay of Fundy view that is always changing and absolutely stunning! The cottage is located in the beautiful Village of Alma, neighbouring community of Fundy National Park.

Alma has an active Wharf that can go from totally quiet to totally busy at the drop of the hat, and it's amazing to watch the boats coming and going, and the hustle and bustle of fisherman as they carry out their days duties, but a person must acknowledge that it is an active, working wharf and as such, must be aware of their surroundings at all times while on or near it .  There are multiple places to eat here during the summer, with the pizza

description:
New in 2023, this quaint new cottage is located on a stunning beachfront property on the warm waters of Northumberland Strait. Facing the incredible sunsets, this cottage is just steps away from the private sandy beach and is perfect for a couple with or without children.

There are many exciting day trip options in New Brunswick for adventurous guests and the property is located within minutes from both PEI and Nova Scotia.

The cottage is fully equipped for your comfort and convenience.
neighborhood_overview: This is a rural fishing and farming community with abundant beaches, close to the bridge to PEI and the border crossing with Nova Scotia at Tidnish and a great jump off point for two national parks, the Dunes at Bouctouche, the Bay of Fundy and the popular Parlee and Aboiteau beaches.
host_about:
I’m a Nova Scotian by birth, with proud Scottish heritage, but now call rural New Brunswick my home. I work as a Financial Planner and host Airbnb guests at my very unique beachfront converted church. 

My objective is for my guests to have a great experience in a sparkling clean, comfortable space, enjoying the beach and huge property and all that the area has to offer.  The area itself is very unique in that fishing and farming exist side by side.  As a result, my guests enjoy the best of country and beachside living.  We are also unique in that we immediately border both PEI and Nova Scotia, so this is an easy jump off point to visit all three provinces.

Our area is famous for the best lobster, oysters, clams and scallops anywhere on the planet. Here, you can take a short drive to the local wharf and buy lobster straight from the fishing boat, at a very reasonable price, and cook it fresh in sea water!

We’ve also got excellent local restaurants serving our area’s best local produce and seafood!

Acadian cultural experiences are nearby, along with the very popular destinations of Hopewell Rocks, Fundy National Park, Kougibouguac National Park, Shediac and Parlee Beach, Aboiteau Wharf and Beach and The Dunes at Bouctouche.  

There is no better place to experience so much, while offering the tranquility of the countryside and the beaches.

name: Riverside Basement Suite
description: This little slice of paradise is nestled at the end of a private lane. My bright and airy basement suite has its own private entrance, with self-check-in ability.  This open concept living area has various amenities including hotplate, fridge, air fryer, 55" tv with premium cable and Firestick along with reliable internet. The breathtaking views of the river can be enjoyed from the large yard. We are very close to the tracks and so trains do go by 3 or 4 times a day. Pets are welcome!
neighborhood_overview: I'm at the end of a private lane, just off the Nerepis Road. There is a church across the street and an elementary school a few yards away, It is private and quiet here on the river. There are ducks that live on the river and even the occasional eagle. In the summer the river is a buzz with boats and there are 5 or 6 that moor close to my place. Also a 5 minute walk from the Westfield Ferry that takes you over to the Kingston Peninsula. It is possible to get down to the beach from my property but it's better suited to goats and dogs! Last summer the water was high so there was not much beach at all. There is a convenience store and eatery a 5 minute walk from here, or  Tim Hortons about a 10 minute drive in the heart of Grandbay. I am 20 minutes from Saint John, and 50 minutes from Fredericton. Conveniently located close to hiway access my place is easy to find.
host_about:
This old house is the love of my life! 

Sharing it with people who can appreciate the location right on the river makes me very happy.

 In the summer you will find me puttering in the yard,  looking for the occasional wayward feline, or picking up after 120lb Archie.
